root_causes.description: Legacy floor shlex-tokenises the whole command text including heredoc bodies; an apostrophe (or unbalanced quote) in a quoted-delimiter body raises ValueError -> <parse-error> -> 'could not parse', although the new heredoc-aware scanner parses the command fine. 16 records (13 by RC1 alone, 3 more need RC1b).
root_causes.narrow_fix: When _legacy_groups fails but _levels() succeeds, do not deny on the floor: run _group_rules over all non-blob levels INCLUDING shell (SCRIPT, body=True) heredoc bodies (which the floor used to see), then the aptly rules as usual; and in that path a SCRIPT body that fails the scanner is a parse error (deny) instead of becoming a blob (676-679). Simulated: 0 regressions on the test lists.

root_causes.description: A git commit/tag -F - heredoc (the commit message) is classified SCRIPT because the owner has operands, so its text is scanned as shell; with an apostrophe it fails the scanner. Records 6, 24, 35.
root_causes.narrow_fix: Classify the body as TEXT when the owner is a git reader whose subcommand is commit or tag with -F -/--file=-/-F /dev/stdin, not piped, level sink_safe, and no output redirection (like _is_sink 612-616 for substitutions).

root_causes.description: python3 -c CODE is always a runner, so string literals in CODE count as aptly mentions and denied words (python -c has no counterpart of the heredoc BLOB rule, which ignores python bodies that cannot start a process). Records 3,4,9,15,19,26,31,34,42,43; C's case (b).
root_causes.guard_location: _is_reader 557-609 (no python -c case), runners 739-740, reach/words/mentions 744-753; compare heredoc BLOB rule 646-647, 669-673 with _STARTS_PROCESS 442-445
root_causes.narrow_fix: In _is_reader treat `python3 -c CODE [args]` as a reader when CODE does not match _STARTS_PROCESS and writes no file other than through json.dump (no .write(, write_text, write_bytes); otherwise keep it a runner. Simulated: clears all 10, 0 regressions.

root_causes.description: Expansion is tracked per level, not per group: $(date) or $D in a reader (echo >> AGENTS-LOG.md, git show) makes the words publish/task/api deny in any exposed runner of the same level, even with no aptly anywhere. Contributes to 4,13,15,26,31,34,43 (all also cleared by RC2/RC4). Documented accepted FP (058 README 443-444).
root_causes.guard_location: _Scanner sets self.expansion for the whole text 129, 142, 274; _collect 342; reach_expansion 746-747; 750-751
root_causes.narrow_fix: Count an expansion only when it sits in an exposed group: record expansion per group (or conservatively: an exposed group whose tokens contain $, SUBST, *, ?, [ or a brace group). Not simulated.

root_causes.description: sed counts as a reader only for p/d/= scripts; any s/// (with or without -i) makes it a runner, which exposes its input/output files' writers and its own script text. Records 11, 13; part of 30.
root_causes.narrow_fix: Also accept sed when every script command is s<d>..<d>..<d> with flags only from [gIip0-9], or p/d/=, separated by ; or newline, options only -n -E -r -i[SUFFIX] -s -z -u; anything unparsed (e, w, W, r, R, flag e/w, -f, --expression) stays a runner. Simulated: 0 regressions.

root_causes.description: The /srv/aptly data-directory exemption applies only when the whole token is that directory path; /srv/aptly inside a larger token (sed script 's|..|/srv/aptly|', --root=/srv/aptly) matches _APTLY_TEXT and is a mention. Record 30; C's case (c).
root_causes.narrow_fix: Before the _APTLY_TEXT search, blank LIVE_APTLY ('/srv/aptly') where followed by end, /, |, :, quote, space, comma, ; ) or ] (the binary itself is still found by _same_as_aptly inode checks). Simulated: 0 regressions.

root_causes.description: awk is not a reader, so a grep for 'aptly' piped into a harmless awk filter is exposed. Record 36.
root_causes.narrow_fix: Treat awk/gawk/mawk as a reader when the only options are -F, there is exactly one program argument and it contains none of system, |, getline, @, ENVIRON, close, or print/printf followed by >. Simulated: 0 regressions.
must_still_deny: awk 'BEGIN{while (("aptly publish list" | getline l) > 0) print l}'

root_causes.description: ssh HOST 'string' is an opaque runner; a plain-reader remote string naming aptly is a mention. Record 10. Already a documented accepted FP (058 README line 442).
root_causes.narrow_fix: Optional, lowest value: parse the ssh remote string (single literal token, no expansion) as a nested level and apply the reader test to it; otherwise keep denying. Recommend leaving as accepted FP. Not simulated.

notes: Backtick inside single quotes is not a problem: 'python3 x.py; sed -i 's/`a`/b/' f' is allowed; the scanner handles it (lines 235-236).
Not a regression but a gap: 'sed -i 's/a/b/w /tmp/s' f; bash /tmp/s' is allowed today and after the fixes (no aptly word).
A python heredoc that writes a script which bash then runs is allowed today (heredoc BLOB without process start is dropped, 669-673); the RC2 fix keeps python3 -c stricter than that.
Current-guard results reproduced only with /srv/aptly present as a directory and /usr/bin/aptly on PATH on builder.
